reason: Single-page neo-Latin epithalamium (1662) by minor author Schaghen for one specific Dutch aristocratic marriage. Ephemeral occasional verse; no English translation found in any catalog/scholarship/web. Our Latin original is fully translated (1/1). Translatable verse, FT-eligible.

Hertel's 1927 German monograph (Leipzig: Haessel, Indo-Iranische Quellen IX) appears in catalogs only in German; cited untranslated in scholarship. English 'Sun/Mithra' hits are canonical Avesta hymns (Khwarshed/Mihr Yasht), a distinct work, not Hertel's interpretive text. No prior English translation found.

Robert Ashley translated his De honore, not this work.

No identified tertón/cycle, no work_id; many unrelated kha byang exist. Identity unresolvable so first-English claim can't be bounded. No prior English found.

Obscure 10-page Ensa-lineage (dben sa snyan brgyud) tshe-sgrub oral-instruction manuscript from the Ogyen Choling Collection (BDRC/EAP). Non-canonical, so out of 84000 scope; no matching title on Lotsawa House/Rigpa/BDRC. Related Hayagriva-longevity sadhanas exist but are distinct works. No prior English of THIS text.

reason: Vol. 4 of the Fifth Dalai Lama's gsan yig 'gangA'i chu rgyun' (Record of Teachings Received, 1670s). Attribution 'Drametse...' is scan source. Only Tibetan eds (Delhi 1971, Sikkim 1991) + Ehrhard's 2012 study (not a translation) exist; no English translation found in BDRC/Sakya/academic sources. Our text partial (25/44 pp, 1 of 4 vols).

Local Bhutanese manuscript (Ogyen Choling Coll., EAP105/Karmay 2003): a byad-'grol curse-liberation/torma-consecration ritual manual with translatable liturgical prose (3/4 pp translated). byad-'grol genre is attested broadly, but no English translation of THIS specific work found on BDRC, Lotsawa House, 84000, or academic sources. Bounded absence.

"dGongs 'dus khrid kyi lde mig" is a key/guidance manual (lde mig) within Pema Lingpa's Kunzang Gongdu treasure cycle, Gangtey Monastery (Bhutan) collection. No English translation of this specific manual found on Lotsawa House, 84000, BDRC, or web; only related scriptures/ngondro notes (distinct works) exist. 220/222 pages translated.

Our book = Deuerling's 1875 Latin edition of the Glossae of (Lactantius/Luctatius) Placidus, a late-antique Latin glossary, with our English translation (121/122 pp). Only Latin scholarly editions exist (Deuerling, Goetz CGL V, Glossaria Latina/Lindsay). No prior English translation found in any catalog.

海國圖志 (Wei Yuan) is a 100-juan gazetteer; our item is juan 19, a coherent prose sub-section. No complete English translation of the work exists; scholarship (Leonard 1984) and Western versions are partial/abridged only. No dedicated full English of juan 19 found.

Hagakure (Yamamoto Tsunetomo, 1716) has many prior English translations: William Scott Wilson (Kodansha, 1979) and Alexander Bennett's complete 11-book translation (2014). Our Vol. 2 (Books 2,5,6,7) is the same work fully covered by these. Not first.

sources_checked: Needham Science and Civilisation in China Vol5 Pt7 Gunpowder Epic (archive.org)
reason: Our item is one fascicle (Wubei Zhi bks 128-130, fire-weapons) of a 240-vol encyclopedia. No complete English Wubei Zhi exists, but Needham's Gunpowder Epic (1986) translates many of these exact fire-weapon entries (poison smoke ball, caltrop fire ball, fire gourd), partly via the parallel Huolongjing. Partial prior English + Huolongjing identity overlap = unresolved.

H-Net review of Bian, Ordering the Myriad Things
reason: Vol. 17 (Stone Herbs/石草類) of Wu Qijun's 1848 Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao; ours fully translated (84/84pp). Sinological sources show only English prefaces + Swingle's unprinted index exist; a Japanese translation exists but no English translation of the text itself. No prior English found.

Nongsang jiyao 農桑輯要 (Yuan agric./sericulture treatise by Sinong Si). Sinological refs (chinaknowledge, ctext), WorldCat, rare-book trade show no complete English translation; only English-language scholarship discusses it as a source. Our record is the Chinese original (vol. 4 of set), no prior English found.

Zhiwu Mingshi Tukao (Wu Qijun, 1848); our book is one juan (vol. 34, Trees) of the original Chinese, fully translated. Sinological sources show only Swingle's indexes + preface translations (Jiang Kanghu/Yuan Tongli) + scattered single-entry studies; no full English translation of the body text exists.

Our item is the Chinese original Wubei Zhi (Mao Yuanyi, 1621), Vol. 77 = the Qimen Dunjia military-divination section (占度載, juan 178-180), fully translated (107/107 pp). The Wubei Zhi was never fully translated to English; existing English work covers different sections (Mao Kun navigation chart, fist canon, weapons). No prior English of this divination section found.

No complete English translation of Zabarella's full 3-book De Anima commentary exists. SEP lists only McCaskey's De methodis/De regressu (different work). Only partial English exists: a 'first ever' translation of the De Mente Agente section (De anima 3.5, agent intellect). Full commentary untranslated.

sources_checked: Project MUSE: Marquis de Sade in English 1800-1850
reason: Sade's Justine (1791) is one of the most-translated French novels. Prior English: censored Risus Press (1930s), first unexpurgated by Wainhouse/Olympia Press (1953), Grove Press (1965). Complete modern English long predates us.

Regiomontanus/Zacuto Ephemerides sive Almanach perpetuum (Santritter ed., Venice 1498) is a Latin astronomical almanac; mostly daily planetary tables plus Latin canons/instructions. No prior English translation found in LoC, Smithsonian, ISTC, or scholarly sources; treated only in Latin. We translated 249/253 pp.

'Superstitions anciennes et modernes' (1733-36, Le Brun/Thiers reworked, Bernard's remarks, Picart engravings) is the French SUPPLEMENT to Ceremonies. The English ed. (7 vols, du Bosc 1733-39) translated only the main Ceremonies (Jews/Catholics/Protestants etc.); no English translation of this Superstitions supplement is recorded.

Work = Bar Hebraeus's Ktaba d-Semhe (Book of Splendours), his great Syriac grammar; our record is the Syriac original (Moberg 1922). Known translations are German (Moberg) + French/Syriac editions only. No English translation of this grammar found in competent Syriac-studies sources. Bar Hebraeus's English-translated works are different texts.

Al-Zamakhshari's Kashshaf (Arabic tafsir, d.1144) is heavily studied in English but the prior English works are studies (Lane/Brill, Kifayat Ullah) and excerpt/introduction translations only — no complete published English translation. Our edition translates the full Arabic commentary (850/852 pp).

Eshel Avraham (Ashkenazi/Rovigo, Fürth 1701; our scan is 1786 reprint) is a Sabbatean Zoharic commentary in Hebrew. Known in scholarship (Scholem, Tishby) and antiquarian trade but no English translation found. Sefaria "Eshel Avraham" is a different halakhic work. Ours is 299/386 pp.

Avodat HaLevi (Pentateuch discourses) by Aaron of Staroselye, Chabad; Hebrew original (Lemberg 1861). No complete English translation found across web/WorldCat/Sefaria. Only excerpts in Louis Jacobs, Seeker of Unity (1966) — a study, not full translation. Distinct from his Sha'arei Avodah/HaYichud.

Our item is Bodleian MS Opp 509 (=Neubauer 1751), an unpublished Hebrew philosophico-kabbalistic commentary on Genesis/Zohar (author refs own Kuzari commentary — likely not Luria himself). Closest English candidate, Klein's Kabbalah of Creation, renders Etz Hayyim's Gate of Principles, a distinct work. No prior English of this MS exists; 513/704 pp translated.

sources_checked: Brill (Musical and Socio-Cultural Anecdotes from Kitab al-Aghani, 2018)
reason: Famous 20+ vol Arabic compendium by al-Isfahani. Scholarship (Wikipedia/Britannica/Brill) confirms NO complete published English translation; only partial English exists (Brill 2018 selected anecdotes; ongoing lyrics-translation project). Our full translation of vols 1-3 (570/574 pp) is first complete.

Contra Impium Grammaticum (vs John the Grammarian) survives in Syriac; standard edition is Lebon's CSCO with a LATIN translation only. No English translation found; Torrance covers different Severan works (Sergius correspondence). Different-source-language Latin prior does not count.

sources_checked: WebSearch: Menasseh ben Israel Misnaioth editions
reason: Our book is Menasseh ben Israel's 1633 Amsterdam printed edition of the complete Mishnah (all 6 orders/60 tractates per chapter list). The underlying work is the canonical Mishnah, first fully translated to English by Danby (Oxford, 1933) from Hebrew, plus later complete versions (Neusner, Soncino, Sefaria). Same work, different edition — not first.

Our book is Nairn's 1904 Greek edition of Herodas' Mimiambi (Mimes), recovered from papyrus in 1891. Multiple prior English translations exist: editions/translations followed the 1891 discovery (Rutherford 1891, Headlam, etc.), and Sharpley's verse translation (1906) confirms an active English tradition. Nairn (1904) is not the first English rendering.

Our book is the Brooke-McLean-Thackeray (1906) Greek critical edition of the Septuagint OT (Genesis). The Greek Septuagint has been translated to English since Brenton (1844, Samuel Bagster), based on the same Codex Vaticanus base text; later NETS (2007) etc. Prior complete English exists.
sources_checked: Wikipedia: The Septuagint version of the Old Testament (Brenton)
Ancient Commentators on Aristotle / Coutant 1936, Lewis 1996
reason: Composite 13th-c Latin manuscript miscellany bundling distinct works: moral aphorisms (De disciplina/De beneficiis), Aristotle/Alexander Meteorology III, and Avicenna De anima chapters. Each has its own transmission and English translation history (Alexander: Coutant 1936/Lewis 1996; Avicenna De anima: from Arabic). A single first-English claim is ill-defined (Rule 5 multi-work container). Not the prior-verdict's "Latin so N/A" ground.

Prior English of this work exists: "The Mirror of Architecture" (W.F., 1669+ eds) renders Book VI via Schuym's Dutch abridgement; and Architectura & Natura Press (2003-08) published direct Italian-to-English translations of Books I, III, VI. Both predate ours.

sources_checked: DK Printworld / Exotic India / Amazon listings
reason: Sadhana Parashar published the first complete English translation of Kavyamimamsa (D.K. Printworld, 2013), translated from the same Sanskrit. Our 1934 Gaekwad ed. (Dalal & Sastry) is the Sanskrit original w/ English notes only. A prior complete English translation exists, so not first.

sources_checked: Indian Journal of History of Science / INSA reference
reason: Our book is the Sanskrit Rasahṛdayatantra of Govinda Bhagavatpāda (Caturbhuja Miśra = commentator; Ācārya = 1911 editor). A complete prior English translation exists: B.V. Subbarayappa, Rasahṛdayatantram of Govinda Bhagavatpāda, Indian J. Hist. Sci. supp. 32 (1997), pp.1-148, INSA. Same work; not first.

道藏目錄詳註 = Bai Yunji's 1626 annotated catalogue of the Ming Daoist Canon (4 juan). No prior English translation found. Wieger's 1911 Bibliographie générale adapted/translated its notes but into FRENCH (doesn't count); Schipper/Verellen 2004 is a distinct modern reference, not a translation. Catalogue-as-container caveat.
sources_checked: Andersen review Study of the Daozang

reason: Boas's "Mythology of the Bella Coola Indians" (1898, Memoirs AMNH v2 pt2) was originally written/published IN ENGLISH by the German-American anthropologist. It is an English ethnographic study (with embedded Nuxalk terms/names), not a Nuxalk-language original we translated. Our "language: Nuxalk" tag is a misclassification. No first-English-translation claim exists.

Pindar's odes (Olympian/Pythian/Nemean/Isthmian) are a canonical Greek classic with many complete prior English translations: Gilbert West (1749), Abraham Moore (1822, full prose), Ernest Myers (1874), etc.—all long before this 1896 Christ critical edition. Different edition, same work.

Balzac's Lettres were repeatedly translated into English from French in the 17th c.: Sir Richard Baker's 'Letters of Monsieur de Balzac' (London 1638; 'New Epistles' vols 2-3; collected 4-part 1654), 'Choyce Letters' 1658, 'Balzac's remaines'. Same work, prior complete English translation predating our 1656 Elzevir French edition.

Our text is Hesiod's Greek Works and Days + Theogony. Prior English from same Greek source long predates us: Chapman translated Works and Days (1618); Cooke's 1728 'Works of Hesiod' was the first complete English incl. the Theogony. Same works, earlier editions.

1475 incunable container: titular Aquinas De articulis fidei (both parts) + De periculis (Parentinis) + De regimine Judaeorum (full prior English, Dyson 2002). Only prior English of titular work is Collins 1939, confirmed Part 2 (sacraments) only; Part 1 (articles of faith) untranslated. Sources conflict on Collins scope; container makes claim ambiguous.

Catena Aurea (Aquinas's catena on the four Gospels) has a famous complete English translation by John Henry Newman, 1841 (Parker/Rivington), still in print in 4 vols. Our Latin Johannes-Andreas edition is the same work. Prior complete English exists.

Our book = Heiberg's 1880 Archimedis Opera Omnia Vol. I (Greek/Latin: On the Sphere & Cylinder I-II, Measurement of a Circle, On Conoids & Spheroids). T.L. Heath, The Works of Archimedes (Cambridge UP, 1897), translated all these into English, using Heiberg's edition as his source text. Clear prior complete English translation.

Work = Maximus' Opuscula Theologica et Polemica (CPG 7697). Only PARTIAL English exists: Louth (Routledge 1996) rendered Opusc. 7 & 3 + scattered article translations of single treatises. Clarke's FIRST COMPLETE English (CUA FOTC vol.150) is forthcoming July 2026, not yet published. No complete prior to date.

De viribus herbarum has a well-documented English translation tradition: John Lelamour's 14th-c. Middle English version, up to nine complete Middle English versions, Frisk's 1949 critical edition (MS), and GUL MS Hunter 497. Prior English translations of this same work positively exist.

Innocent III's De miseria humanae conditionis is a famous medieval Latin text with a long English-translation history: Chaucer's lost version (1384-95), Gascoigne's Droomme of Doomes-day (1576), and complete modern translations by Howard/Dietz (1969) and Lewis (1978). Our 1470 Latin incunable is the same work; prior English clearly exists.

Aldine 1513 editio princeps = Plato's complete works (opera omnia): 30+ distinct dialogues (Republic I-X, Timaeus, Critias, Laws, Epinomis, Axiochus, Eryxias, Letters, Definitions, etc.). A single 'first English translation' claim is ill-defined for a multi-work container; each dialogue has its own long-standing English history.

Vol. I of the Brunschvicg/Boutroux/Gazier critical edition (Grands Ecrivains de la France) — a multi-work scholarly container: original 1900s editorial apparatus + an anthology of Pascal early works/letters + family memoirs. First-English claim is ill-defined; component works (minor works via Wight/Harvard Classics 1910; Gilberte Perier's Life) already exist in English.

Phillip De Lacy's complete English translation 'Galen: On the Doctrines of Hippocrates and Plato' (Corpus Medicorum Graecorum V 4,1,2; Akademie Verlag 1978-84) covers all nine books. De Lacy translated from Greek; our scan is the Latin edition, but the work is identical, so a prior English exists.

Only prior English is Mathers' 'The Kabbalah Unveiled' (1887), explicitly PARTIAL: just 3 Zohar tracts (~330pp) from Knorr's Latin. No complete English of the whole 2-vol Kabbala Denudata exists. Our scan (2528/2547 pp translated) covers the full work incl. dissertations, Pneumatica, De Anima, etc.

A complete English translation was published 1548-49 (Udall, Coverdale, Catherine Parr et al.); Vol. 2 (1549) = "the Epistles and other NT writings", placed in every English parish. Prior complete English from same Latin source exists.

Al-Futuhat al-Makkiyya has substantial prior English translations of this exact work: Chodkiewicz ed. 'The Meccan Revelations: Selected Texts' (Pir Press, Eng. 2002, from 1988 bilingual), Chittick's Sufi Path of Knowledge (1989) / Self-Disclosure of God (1998), and Haj Yousef's ongoing series. No complete English exists, but our text is also only partial — so not first complete.

Arabic Kalila wa Dimna by Ibn al-Muqaffa has abundant prior English translation: Wyndham Knatchbull (1819, from De Sacy's Arabic) and a complete modern Library of Arabic Literature edition (Fishbein & Montgomery, 2021) both translate this exact Arabic work. Not first.

sources_checked: Wikipedia: The Book of Fixed Stars
reason: Ihsan Hafez's 2010 James Cook University PhD thesis is documented as the first complete English translation of al-Sufi's Suwar al-kawakib (from Arabic). Same work, same source language, prior English exists. Schjellerup (1874) was French. Our record is a 1-page item.

Our book is Vol. 5 of Saikaku's Koshoku Ichidai Otoko (1682). A prior English translation of this novel exists: Kengi Hamada, 'The Life of an Amorous Man' (Charles E. Tuttle, 1964), covering the full work. Prior English positively found; our item is one volume of that novel.

Qimin Yaoshu (Jia Sixie, 6th c.), our Chinese original. Prior English exists but only partial: Shih Sheng-han's 'Preliminary Survey of Ch'i Min Yao Shu' (1962/1974) + Bray's selections in SCC vol.6.2 (1984); scholars note ongoing partial efforts. No complete English of all 92 chapters attested.

Qimin Yaoshu (Jia Sixie, c.544 CE). Only prior English is Shih Sheng-han's 1974 'A Preliminary Survey of Ch'i Min Yao Shu' — annotated excerpts, explicitly partial. No complete English translation cataloged (WorldCat shows only Chinese modern translations, e.g. Miao Qiyu). Thus first complete English.

Mengxi Bitan (Dream Pool Essays) by Shen Kuo has a documented English translation history: partial translations via Needham's Science and Civilisation in China (1950s+) and the first complete English translation, Brush Talks from Dream Brook (Wang Hong & Zhao Zheng, 2008). Prior English exists.

Tirukkural is among the most-translated works ever. English translations long predate our 1840 Tamil edition: Kindersley 1794 (partial), Ellis 1812, Drew 1840, complete verse by G.U. Pope 1886. Same work, different edition; many prior complete English translations exist.

sources_checked: ResearchGate: Editions and Translations of Avicenna's Canon
reason: Avicenna's al-Qanun has prior published English translations: O.C. Gruner's Book I (1930, from the Latin) and M.H. Shah's Book I (1964); Bakhtiar's multi-volume set later. Same work, prior English exists. Source-language rule: Gruner's Latin-based English still counts.
